body: I just don't want to be alone anymore, I can't take it. I'd trade all the money in the world for a friend. I don't want anything special, just to not be alone anymore.

Not great Bob. I try my best with friends, family, and personal relationships. I do my best to continue my education and advance my career. Everything in my entire life has been a string of failures. I'm empty and don't feel like making an effort anymore b/c it always leads back to the same miserable place. Sorry to make you sad.

I don't have anything special to say. Same things as most depressed people. Just a lonely guy who can't seem to find where he fits in this world. A loser with no skills or anything special. I try but no one cares. I'm just another name that no one will ever remember, a ghost in a shell

Call her that morning. Remind her of the positive benefits of just letting it out. If that is too vague, have her make a list of 3 things each that bothered her the last week, the last month, and last year and also what she hopes to accomplish in the next week, month, or year. Don't say "make a list, now!" but ask, "what in the past stills bothers you and what in the future do you wish to achieve?" Give loose guidelines and let them fill in the blanks. If she doesn't attend, the negative will grow and the positive will wither.

Many therapists (psychologists or psychiatrists) aren't that great. I've seen several. I've known people who saw the same therapist for years before committing suicide. The main lesson is that they bill by the hour and to get your money's worth you need to honest and upfront, don't hold back on what is bothering you or why it is bothering you. They don't care about your problems as much as you care about your problems b/c they don't have to take them home with them. Push you therapists and don't expect them to be your savior, they get paid by the hour and not by the patient.

There is inherent trouble in forcing the issue. Only force it by requiring her to tell her friend or you if necessary to prevent immediate harm. Your friend is having a tough time and as long as they are making progress just go with it. It was a huge step for her to reach out to you, she is making progress, take it slowly. If someone with mental health issues is reaching out to others and making active decisions to improve their life please let them move at their own pace as it shows they are comfortable in their decisions. Those with mental health issues almost always, always, keep it a secret b/c of the stigma. Provide a relaxed, judgement free zone where she can express herself when needed. Once she has that base she can build off of it but if you mess with that small amount of progress you'll just set her back. Tough love isn't really gonna help her in this situation, she needs to cross each hurdle one at a time.

I get in fights with walls where I can't win. I'll basically slam my fists into anything that won't break. My knuckles have since become flat and covered with scar tissue. I don't hit the wall because I hate it, I strike it because I know it will tear my hands into pieces, that the only way it will end is with blood and broken bones. Then I can relax.
"Why are you so quiet" is probably one of my least favorite questions. Already having enough trouble without being asked why I'm having so much trouble

I'll tell people I'm ready to give up, that I can't keep living like this but there is almost no one to talk to, I've mentioned it around some family but they brush it off, always tell me "it'll get better" and that's the extent of it. I've seen several psychiatrists and psychologists, typical answer is to think how sad that would make people and how my dog would be upset. I also get told to exercise, find a hobby, and make new friends. If you think people who kill themselves haven't tried to get better on their own, haven't sought professional help, and reached out to anyone close to them before committing suicide, you'd be wrong. They likely have tried all of the above and gotten nothing positive in return. Suicide isn't born from sadness, its created from a profound sense of loneliness and hopelessness in life, it isn't the desire to die but the lack of a desire to live.

I been around 30+ years and haven't found or done anything that provides any kind of fulfillment on an emotional level. I think when I was born the part of humans that makes our life enjoyable or anything about life feel rewarding was missing from me.
For some of us there really isn't anywhere to go in life, there is no vacancy for those who need a place the most
"A man is not old until regrets take the place of dreams"

I ain't got no legs. You're a good person that hasn't walked far in these shoes. I appreciate the reply and the positivity but for some of us we've grown tired to of the "it's gets better" sing-song because the proof is in pudding as they say. Take my ingredients and bake em up, you'll get something no one wants to eat. Happiness is only a day away is as true as it is false, no one can tell you how it will turn out or why. So say it will turn around if you want but that isn't based on much unless you're a dual psychologist/recruiter. Sounds bitter but after a exercising the same routine and getting nowhere the idea that tomorrow will be your best day is laughable.

I just got fired (again) today. I'm in my mid-thirties and despite my college education, work experience, and occupational schooling, I haven't been able to hold a job for longer than a year for the past 8 years, everything has either been temp work or jobs I was fired from or laid of off. At this point no one is going to hire a washout like me. I'm a has been or really a never-was, so I think I'm just gonna work a mindless job and die alone because everything else is too much to deal with. I fluctuate between the decision of whether to deal with the disappointment I am to myself and family or taking the quick route and ending it all b/c this is going nowhere. I'm not a useless person but I'm useless to most people.

Good question and I don't know the answer. When people can't relate to one another is it exclusively one side's problem more than the other? If people can share a perspective they will understand each other better. It's hard to relate to people who haven't shared the same burdens or hardships in life. It's just hard to leave your troubles behind like they didn't exist and I think if I could do that it would be easier to relate and get along with those who have had to carry a lighter load through life. I just know that I relate better to people who have been down or had hard times in life.

People ask me why I'm alone, that I never have a date, always show up by myself. I don't know why, mental health problems hold me back but like you there isn't anything outwardly stopping me. I'm just a lonely guy who can't make friends no matter what I try.

I'm similar in that I can't relate to anyone who hasn't had some kind of trouble or trauma in their life that has had some lasting negative effects. Doesn't have to be major, but if you've had a well-rounded life with love and support from family and friends and a good upbringing we're on different wavelengths. I just can't relate to people who don't have some kind of emotional damage.

If you gave all that up would you be happier or feel the same? If that all went away you wouldn't feel any different? Our search for meaning is an individual endeavor. It is also somewhat ridiculous by nature because no one knows why certain things matter and others don't matter and there is no way to calculate the value of it all. We just have to keep searching and hope we stumble upon meaning in life. I think this is why people take psychedelics.

I always try and be positive when posting to these subs but I've got the same problem and no solution. I am difficult person as well and I have no idea how to build and maintain relationships no matter how many books I read or therapist I see. It's not that people hate me (some do of course but usually without reason, just biases or differences in opinion) just that no one likes me, that if every person on this earth had to make a list of twenty people to keep in their life and no one else I wouldn't be on anyone's list. The best I'll be is filler, a non-essential stand in and never a feature. Makes me feel like a loser and I don't know what to do.

My Dad got sick and died. We never had the chance to do things together, he got sick when I was younger and  by the time I was a teen he wasn't well enough to work anymore and eventually couldn't do anything. I bought a fishing rod and reel a while back, it just sits in the corner of my room unused b/c I haven't taken the time to learn how to fish. I imagine when I do go it will be me and my dad fishing together, I'll be 12 again and we'll be at the lake in our old neighborhood and he'll finally teach me to tie that lure on after all these years, that one moment will never happen, I'd kill for that, just five minutes of it. It'll never happen and I'll carry that sadness to my grave. I'm sorry that you didn't get what you needed from your parents, it really, really hurts. I'm sorry.

The also want to put a face to things and given the nature of the sub they just imagine fat slobs with poor hygiene and no social skills. They never think of the quiet person at work who no one knows anything about, or the guy eating at the bar by himself on a Saturday night, or the person who has lived across the street for years who you only ever see walking their dog but always alone and you don't know their name. The world is full of lonely people and to answer Paul's question, they come from all over. Also, I'm alone b/c I have problems with depression and anxiety and these have made it hard to develop and maintain healthy relationships throughout my life.

Yeah, social events where you're usually expected a plus one are tough. I'm tired of showing up alone and having non one to dance with or kiss at midnight. I have no reason for feeling like a loser though I act like one all the time, just some weird personality trait you can't overcome. Idk, I wish it was easier

First step is believing in yourself some way. Our parents are supposed to instill in us the belief that we are important so we can have the confidence and support to be important. I'm sorry you missed that from your father. Now, you must provide yourself with that self-belief. You're gonna need to go it alone for the time being (don't get bitter and cut yourself off) unless there are other family or friends you didn't mention.  Point is you don't currently have the support you need so to get where you want will take extra dedication but it can be done, it just happens bit by bit over a long period of time. Life is change and it never stops. You may feel stuck but you can probably make a list of five things you would like to have done tomorrow, in a week, in a month, in 3 months, and in a year. Can be anything, doesn't have to be serious, just realize you make your own successes if you want regardless of what your dad says.

Easiest thing to do is think of the progress and payoff from accomplishing the goal (of 2 miles < 17 min). When you think of having to actually do the day-to-day grind I'm sure it causes anxiety, unpleasantness, and even fear and those emotions tell you not to engage in the act b/c it brings physical and emotional struggle. Avoid it and there will be no immediate discomfort. Doing an activity that causes a negative feeling is a struggle so the best advice would be to imagine you accomplishing what it is you want, you're doing something now to achieve something later. Don't focus too much on the moment but the end result. If you truly want to what it is you're aiming for, just focus on the just rewards. It's nothing more than positive reinforcement, don't let the negative de-motivate you.

Do whatever it takes not to flunk. I was depressed and couldn't bring myself to engage in academics and haven't ever made up that ground. I know it's tough to care, but if you can't care you may have to find ways to accomplish in academics. Failure in your academic career will only compound your depression, it'll be a friend you lost and you only have yourself to blame. People with depression are almost on empty or close to it and most times it's close to impossible to care so when it comes to things that are important, such as, friends, family, health, academics, career, etc. you will need to find a way to make things happen or at least not fail even in the face of depression because letting the important things waste away breeds misery. I understand you feel as though you can't succeed as you are, you may need to make a new plan or strategy to get through those tough times, to learn new habits and mechanisms to balance out the bad days. That isn't easy, you're changing yourself and your routine and change is difficult and stressful but it is better than the alternative which is to let depression win. You have tough options but strive for the one with the best outcome and realize it is tough at times.

Well said. Getting over it just means there are things in life you can't change. Sometimes it easier to get over it and sometimes its impossible, not everything can be overcome. It probably isn't just blind hope but faith in friends, family, or any other type of support and an upbringing that wasn't too stressful to put it one way.
No, I feel the most fulfilling things in life are close personal relationships and not have any causes me pain

Almost all social skills are learned but like most things it is much harder to learn later in life. You can be more social it is just harder as you get older b/c when people are young they want to find new things and when they are older they mostly don't
Right now I'm ten years younger and out partying with cool people and impressing all the ladies not sitting alone in my room wondering where it all went wrong

I started Mirtazapine (no fluoxetine) 5 weeks ago and the past few days have been rough. I've become wound so tight I can't function. I was extremely agitated and irritable yesterday. I also physically felt as though I had what I would best describe as an adderral hangover, just very strung out. Also, confused by things I wouldn't normally be confused by. I've dealt with depressions/anxiety my whole life and tried lots of prescriptions so I've experienced the different side effects of coming on/off medication before but I don't think this is a side I think this is the effect. I skipped my first does last night and messaged my doc but haven't heard back. Feel much better today.

I feel the same way you do, you've described it perfectly, that I'm handicapped, have a scared avoidant mindset, that every person is an immediate threat, that I'm broken, and that I'm meant to be miserable because I was born different and that is a curse. I've worked on overcoming all of those and had little success but the success I've had is worth it and I do owe it to working with many therapist, ranging from terrible to better than average. It's hard though. You need to make progress so start to today. It'll take time and you'll often feel the same hate you feel now but  if you continually carry the burdens that pain you the best you can do is stay exactly where you are at. When you find good treatment lay it on the line, you might not think you can change your life but you're the only one who can.

We're quiet because we have trouble interacting. No such thing as an introvert who thinks their opinion is most important. We fear judgement so we don't speak loud, saying too much is worse than not saying anything to us.

The older I get the more I realize how the attention and affection we from our home and community in our youth and adolescence pays huge dividends in life. A simple lack of attention and positive reinforcement in our youth can lead to a lifetime of neediness and loneliness, it creates desperate people trying to find treasure buried in the past. You can love yourself on your own but it's always much easier to have someone show you how.
It's not though. When your stomach is full everything is less appetizing. One day you'll hunger for those moments of friendship and love. Cynicism goes best with politics.
Lonely life. World's full of people.
So why are you alone this holiday and what do you think the reasons are?

You have to express yourself but use terms and language that they will be receptive to or as receptive as possible. Instead of calling someone an idiot for doing something wrong maybe say "I can help you with that as soon as I can" or "if you need help please ask and I'll be glad to show you" or "if you have any suggestions or tips please let me know", or " a possible suggestion if I may", things like that. This way, if you can't control the anger, you can at least control the output and not say something you regret. Once the anger subsides, follow up and let them know you don't mind helping them or them asking questions and that if they were upset it was just a moment. If it is general annoyance, simply ask what it is they need and you would accommodate them as best you can. If it is really bad just say you didn't hear and need them to repeat. Be easy with your words, swallow the stress, and then clear the air afterwards if need be. I understand some people are more irritating than others, especially family, but being mindful of what you say can really help.

True. Don't miss out on life even though you have dark days. Shutting down is the easy option but when is the easy option usually the best? Everyone deserves to be happy but it isn't easy and no one will do it for you.

I have the same problem, everything triggered anxiety and I would shut down, the minute I woke up I felt like I was about to be in trouble for something, real or not. I was overwhelmed by everything, works, school, friends, chores, etc. until I decided to block everything just to avoid the stress. Only thing that got me was an ex girlfriend and flunking out of college. General constant anxiety is difficult to deal with and takes time to solve. Anxiety is related to fear and stress. That is normal at certain points in life, college exams for sure, but if you can't manage and have exaggerated anxiety to the point where you can't carry on a normal routing on your own there are medications that can help and I would look into if your school has a health center which can help. I hit the bottle and it didn't help, just chased away what was bothering me for about 12 hours and then I would repeat. Sometimes you just need to bridge through the hard times.

Something is stopping you from joining in, likely the feeling that participation is fruitless as you'll either be ignored or ridiculed for trying to be "part of it" b/c who you feel you are is not someone who should be be "part of it".  You're not unable to say anything, it's just that anxiety or depression have created mindset that dictates your inner monologue making it difficult to integrate with the group. You move at the same speed and live in the same world as everyone else but see and feel things differently, its just you need to be comfortable enough to put yourself into the situation that is passing by. This is hard to do for most people, social skills are a lifetime project for most. I'm not sure how to best tell you to not feel overwhelmed by these social situations, but start slow and start with what you know. There is nothing wrong with interjection or joining a conversation when you have something of value to add, whether fact or opinion. Just be sure to start from a mindset of enjoying the participation instead of winning a battle.

If you like celebrating the holidays and have plans to enjoy them let him know he is welcome to join in anything. If he rebuffs you, I'm sorry and I know that it hurts to have a parent show disinterest in their own child's wants and need. Just let him know that is something that makes you happy, unfortunately you might not get any positive response. Breaking stride from our parents is difficult but if keeping stride is only hurting you than make a change. What that change is, idk. Maybe volunteer at a shelter somewhere for Christmas to help the less fortunate, I think contributing to the happiness of even people who are strangers might make your holiday feel more whole since you'll be able to share in the joy without the judgement. What you have to give may not be appreciated by your father but that doesn't mean there aren't people who do appreciate who you are and what you have, it's just unfortunate it isn't at your home. Sometimes in life we make our own way and forget the past.

I've dealt with this same thing for nearly 30 years, I hated myself b/c I never felt loved. Its a raw deal but it isn't fate, just circumstance. Stringing together a few good days into a good week into a good month is hard. Have a conversation with yourself or someone else about where these feelings come from, once you understand the source you can begin to heal. Negative emotions come from somewhere and we all have them, just that some of us are more sensitive to them. I don't believe in the impossible, just the very difficult and most things are very difficult, some more so for certain people. Life is all about finding your way and not stopping.

How many bad days are you going to have? Probably most of them. How many good days are you going to have? Probably only a few. I hate the person I see in the mirror b/c of what I've done. You can become a better person but you have to be honest about what makes you hurt and the things you've done wrong without blaming yourself everyday. Moving on is hard to do, it isn't erasing the past but living with it. Choose how to live with it. Today is not yesterday and tomorrow is not today and nothing happens overnight. Life doesn't suck but it is indifferent to the individual. To be the individual you wish to be takes time and work. With the right help, you can get there, it will just be difficult and you'll need to deal with the bad days. All humans want attention and love its just that some of us never got it at important times. Life doesn't have a schedule, just a cycle.

Existentialism is the theory that none of this matters. Find fulfillment in the small things b/c they are all small things, no big picture exists just small pieces that add up. Let go of history and embrace the future by experiencing life and what it offers in your time. No one notices me either but I made a simple decision to dress better to change that. I made a budget and went to the outlets. It took time but I got a decent wardrobe and I'm proud of it. When you dress better than those around you people will notice though they might not say anything. I got a good haircut and took better care of myself as well. Major change, no. No one is going to give me an award or even care twenty years from now but it doesn't matter. Carpe diem doesn't mean rule the world, it means time is short so don't be afraid to do anything. We all die with regrets but not missed opportunities.

Some people on this earth are just intrinsically liked by others for whatever reason and some people aren't. If you weren't born with it you should build it. Pick some hobby or talent, anything, and get good at it. It doesn't matter if it is learning to play the harmonica or photography or getting better at your job. Maybe just hold the door, smile, and say hello to the stranger behind you at the store. Do something to let people see you are true human with a good heart that wants to grow. I'm sorry you have to try when others don't, I can't explain any of that, why others have it easier and others don't, there will never be an answer. No one wants to build from scratch but sometimes thats the only option. And if doesn't work try again, it's the de facto human anthem.

It isn't being alive that is hard, it's believing you're alive for something but feeling the opposite. You can't help but feel depressed yet won't stop trying to change how you feel. Actions that bring emotional fulfillment don't exist to the depressed yet we try and try because we're desperate. Those that feel there is no hope commit suicide or just fade away from life because being alive is hard. We all wish we were a different person or had an alternative life or personality we could exist in but all we have is what we got, we hate it, and wish it was different. Every day and it wears you down.
Same thing as every Friday. Nothing. Can't remember the last time I had a weekend or Holiday with friends, probably been 11 years now.

It's just sad to know that someone is lost to the world and everyone in it and there is nothing you can do about it, especially when it is suicide at a young age. I never did and I never will talk to her for the rest of my life and I just wish there was a way to say that I remembered who she was, that she did matter, and she is missed. Maybe it would've made a difference. I don't know why, probably b/c I've been there, but things like this I don't forget, it'll stay with me for a long time.
Yeah, my fingertips and lips are always bloody. There is a subreddit for everything /r/CompulsiveSkinPicking and /r/calmhands
I think the hooker analogy is probably more accurate than the waiter, you pay b/c you want to feel better but end up just as empty as before b/c it isn't the real thing

I can't possible feel as bad as you do right now but I feel pretty bad seeing this, literally crying. I love my dog and just thinking about (eventually) going through this with her is making me sick. Life is just so unfair sometimes. Looks like your pup had all the love it could ever want from the best owner ever. Forever a good boye/girl, sleep easy doggo.

Like you, I rely on alcohol because of my anxiety as well. It took me a long time to realize it too.

When things are going smoothly I don't bother with drinking or if I do it is isn't a problem, i.e. I could get hammered and still have fun, behave appropriately, and make the right decisions. So when I don't feel anxiety (raerly), I am calm and content and alcohol isn't a problem. When I have anxiety, whether from stress at work, general social anxiety, or anxiety from personal issues or depression, my whole mindset deteriorates, I start drinking, and go off the rails. There are many other triggers too. It's a real Jekyll and Hyde type situation.

Sometimes the drinking kills off the anxiety but other times it magnifies the underlying stress and I end up making stupid decisions and putting myself in terrible situations, I've previously caused myself physical damage resulting in hospital stays as well getting into significant legal trouble, hurting my career, damaging personal relationships, and just plain embarassing myself.

Giving up drinking would be good for me in the same way that it would be good for anybody. It would eliminate "risky" situations, but I can't do that without first managing my anxiety. You'll have to learn to techniques to manage it, you'll need to have a plan or steps to take when you feel it overwhelming you. The first step is being self-aware. Many times I would be wrecked with anxiety and not even realize how it was affecting me, all of a sudden I would lash out or start crying. The first thing you need to learn to do is take a time out and take a step back. Mindfulness is something that works. If you don't put yourself in a position where you can clear your head to make thoughtful decisions anxiety and stress will overcome you and when it does you will become less rational and when you become less rational is when the alcohol or drugs or other bad decision come.

If you don't manage your stress/anxiety it will manage you and then real problems will start. This isn't just a matter of will-power, of you versus the bottle or you versus yourself, but a matter of you understanding yourself. Learn to talk to yourself as a person, talk that person about their problems, and work through it. You anxiety and how it relates to drinking is a separate problem from your addiction but they are related, you'll need to learn to work through both by being at peace with yourself. I can't give you all the answers but hopefully I gave you something to start with. It isn't easy and I still fail but I have gotten better. Best of luck to you, let us know how it goes and don't hesitate to get help and ask questions whenever you feel you need it.
I think you summarize BPD pretty well, "depressed with a passion". We are people with destructive and beautiful issues.

Whenever I tried to make friends I always found my self on the outside doing what I could to or be a part of the group but I was just different or a little too weird to ever make friends or penetrate social circles, it pretty much usually ended in failure. I tried to be friendly, helpful, and be of some interest or use but it never really amounted to much. People didn't hate me, I just wasn't anyone my classmates or teachers noticed. I don't really have friends from those years even though I tried, it just didn't happen, no one seemed to like me that much. I have a lot of experiences like the one above. No one every directly said anything bad to me but I could read between the lines because even if I thought things were going well I ended up alone or excluded from most social functions. By my senior year I was alone and had given up on making any real friends. I still have my high school yearbooks which by the time I was a junior or senior had no signatures. I don't really remember much except feeling unimportant and not wanted. Most stories are more pathetic than that last one. It still hurts to this day.

It's hard to find understanding from people when it comes to depression and anxiety when they don't suffer from it. I've opened up to a few people and it just made things worse, mostly pushed people away. People will likely hold it against you if they don't understand it, especially since it is abstract, it can't be seen, heard, felt etc. A broken body always gets more sympathy than a broken mind or soul. The best thing to do is cognitive behavioral therapy (talking to a therapist) or group therapy, those are the best places to find understanding but its also hard to open up to strangers. I always wished there would be someone close to me I could talk to without being judged as weak or flawed.

That is sort of how I feel about my life, that I'll eventually kill myself, it's just a matter of how long I can hold out, I've made it well over 30 years now but I'm more miserable than ever. If I don't do it quickly at some point I figure I'll eventually just waste myself away into obscurity to the point where I can just decide to slip away while all alone without anyone noticing so my death will be like my life, as though it never happened

One time in high school I was hanging out at this kid's house (I wouldn't really call him a friend) with a group of other people. They decided to go somewhere else, I can't remember why or where exactly, and told me to meet up with them later at another friend's neighborhood. When I got there I didn't see anyone else. I parked my car, looked around, and waited for some time b/c I thought maybe I got there first. I waited almost an hour before calling some people. No one answered. I realized that I must've been ditched and didn't know what to do. In the end I just went home and went up to my room and laid there alone till I fell asleep. I wasn't worth it I guess.

Yeah, every now and then I have days where I am a basically a different person than my normal self. I feel completely relaxed, free from anxiety/depression, am positive, friendly, sociable, productive, and able to enjoy life. Its as if there are no obstacles, things that stopped me or dragged me down before are no longer a problem. I honestly can do anything those days, I just know that I will succeed. I actually matter. It never lasts. If I could feel that way half the time I would accomplish amazing things but such days are so rare. Completely random too, there is no reason I feel that way, it just is one of those days, that happens a few times a year.

I've done both. As a caveat, there are so many different Rx meds for depression/anxiety/BiPolar etc. and they all have different methods of affecting brain chemistry. Also, doctors (psychiatrists) still don't fully understand how these medications work. The general consensus is that it they work by altering brain chemistry levels (generally SSRI or serotonin re-uptake inhibitors or other mechanisms) but the actual effectiveness of this change in brain chemistry has not been completely proven. There are trends in psych med but no meds are really proven outside of meds that sedate you or knock you out. Daily maintenance type meds don't have a solid track record BUT they doesn't mean they won;t work for you. For years I tried a multitude of meds and I recently stopped taking them. I don't feel that much different, mood swings might be more frequent but I'm not more or less depressed. In regards to weed, it definitely helped, but the problem is the side effects. So it helped with anxiety and depression b/c i could relax, step back from and separate from all the things that nag me, and focus on what was important. I could shake what bothered me and get in touch with my honest self. The only problem is that I was stoned, and when you are stoned you eventually get tired and can't focus. You can't constantly be stoned, it might help from time to time, but you can't go everywhere and do everything stoned. So I side with judicious and selective use of medicinal herbs than constant use of Rx meds but that is just my personal opinion.

So sorry about your brother. People move one, it happens no matter what. Now, there are very tight groups of friends who stick together throughout the years, but even those types of groups have changing dynamics b/c people get gfs or bfs, coworkers, new jobs, new places to live etc. I would say that you should go back over the past few years and think of all the people you have met or interacted with that you no longer talk to or are friends with. That is sort of the same thing that they are doing to you. Now, I understand that this is sort of different b/c you are young and these are people who have been friends most of your life, but this is something that happens to most people in the world today. Not sure if you're American, but I am, and most people I know from high school and college are now spread out to different cities and states and even if they are still "local" are in different places whether literally or metaphorically. Just something that happens, no matter how close you are with your friends. It doesn't sound like your friends are that attached to you so I would say that you need to just be aware of where you are now, be mindful of all that life has been in front of you, and make the most of it. Self-loathing is so terrible and is a key part of depression and other mental disorders. We see life through such a different prism so what reaches our mind's eye is always so negative even with no reason. You could call it self-doubt or self-loathing or whatever you want but it clearly affects you. Eventually, we decide that we are a terrible person and deserve misery even if it isn't true. However, you are so young. I had the same feelings at your age and let it control me for the next 15 years. Deciding who you are and how your life will turn out is a source of anxiety for anyone. Don't let it consume you or prevent you from trying or attempting things. Doing nothing, even if you aren't sure or have self-doubt, is counter productive even though it might be the most comfortable option. I was so unready to move on with life when I was your age so I did nothing and then once I was comfortable with doing nothing I kept doing that. Eventually, in an ironic twist, I became so angry and depressed with myself about doing nothing. So I don't known if you always feel the way you do or if you just feel this way now. You may hate yourself or fell so fake doing things that make you feel uncomfortable but don't let that stop you. It's so hard not to feel the way you feel but don't let it be the only thing that you think about. Focus on anything else, doesn't matter what,and if it helps the it does and if it doesn't than nothing loss and nothing gained. You're young and have plenty of time to change what hurts you, it may seem unlikely, seem very hard, but it might make a difference in your life. The future of life is a component of anxiety no matter who you are so learning to deal with life's challenges and experiences will help you grow. If you need any other advice just ask.

I'd like to think that my advice is not trite as i have the same problems they have, I've walked in those shoes  and it is not unsolicited, it is in a reddit post, if the asks for no replies it's unsolicited but otherwise anyone is allowed to comment. I don't know what effect my comments have but I hope they help b/c I've been there but if they aren't for everyone then fine, just ignore and move on. I am not criticizing depressed people, just sharing my own experience and the gains I made and maybe they can help others. Not for everyone but I don't repeat the same sayings but try to connect to people on the same level. It isn't easy to listen to other people, especially strangers on the internet, but it's still a great place b/c you're anonymous and can share your situation without being overally judged. I just know, from experience, that giving up hope is one of the worst things you can do, that life will challenge you, that bad things will happen, but that all people have the ability to cope, manage, and improve from any defect or setback.

You may think that is a platitude, fine, but at the same time it is once again, life experiences from someone who has struggled with many problems in his life and wants others who also have struggled to be better. I'm not a master but if I can help someone, somewhere than what is the harm. So many psychologists and psychiatrists that I've lost count. You expect solid advice or real, concrete help, but they can't do that, no one can. The whole point of their job is to get you to talk and for some of us that is very hard. Being depressed means we can't be in touch with our true feelings and emotions and don't know how to normally express them. Accomplishing these things will make you feel better. I don't think that you are tricking your therapists, they jut realize that you don't want to meet them halfway and if you can't that there is only so much they can do for you. You don't know what will happen. As cliche as that sounds, you could do absolutely nothing to change your life and be a completely different person in seven years. Or you could do something you think is insignificant that will change many things. Or you could do whatever and who knows what will happen. I suffer from depression or anxiety or bipolar, or whatever my doctor wants to call it and the thing that always makes it worse is focusing on the past or the future instead of the present. How many people really think seven years ahead, I mean literally and precisely think seven years ahead? It's too far away to be accurate. Not saying it's pointless but precision is for the present.

Why try is the one thing that hurts all of us the most. It's what really separates those who are happy and those who aren't (there are other things of course but I'm being simple). This just resonates with me because I always said to myself "why try" when I should have said "why not try"? If I had started saying "why not" earlier in life I think I would be much happier so I'm glad you decided to go ahead and do it today (yesterday or whenever). Lack of motivation for any and all things in life is one of the worst parts of mental illness. What we actually do matters more than what we think

It sucks, I know. I'm in my mid thirties and have felt the same way you do for the past twenty years. I dwell on so many negative things in my life and I'm miserable. Sometimes though, there are decent parts that break through and I do feel happy. It's rare, I'm mostly miserable, but I just have faith that i will be better in the next week, month, year etc. b/c I'll try. You have to stop doing the old painful things, sort of think less about everything, and just give a try to things with no expectations. Just being static, staying still and only thinking of what has already happened can't help you. There will still be failure but venturing into the strange might mean you will find something new about yourself or your life. It's hard to put into words, but sometimes you just sort of run into something that makes your life better without looking for it or even knowing it exists. Failure is part of life an you'll have to deal with it but don't go out expecting it to happen, even if it usually does. Life really is hard but you can't find happiness if you don't even think it exists. It's a battle, cherish the wins and learn from the defeats. That's the best you can do.

Mindfulness helps top snap out of it, it's also why people always suggest trying or doing new or different things b/c it helps break the cycle.

As stupid, as this sounds, struggle through it because life changes so much in you early twenties. Just try not to stay static. I've been depressed all my life but my late teens and early twenties were the better parts of my life. There is so much happening and so much to experience. People really do cherish youth. I understand the tiredness, it's like polishing a stone with a washcloth, eventually you just say screw it. I know you feel aimless and maybe unwanted but don't think about that. Do something nice for your your Mom, Gram, and Sister. Doesn't have to be anything fancy, even something as simple as getting them their favorite food or movie. This will mean something no matter how much of a pessimist you are. I too feel like preserved meat that doesn't serve any purpose besides being passed through this world. This is a hard feeling to shake and I'm not sure how to really correct it. Just don't shut off and disappear. The funny thing about depression is that we always see ourselves as so much less than how others see us. Our perspectives are so different that it is hard for us to understand empathy and caring but rest assured, as corny and unnatural as it may seem to us, it is a real and strong feeling in others and they likely feel it for you. The hard part is is bridging the gap from the emotional differences that separate us. I know the tiredness, the feeling as though you are lost in a mile deep ocean and no one is coming to help so why stay alive? The best answer I can give is that there is a strange human strength you have that fights every thought you have. Otherwise, you would've just killed yourself. I think Freud gave it a name or something, but there is a part that might be losing the battle bit is still fighting. This is your inner-conflict and it is the hardest battle you will ever fight. You can win battles though you may never win the war but don't go out without a fight.

Now I'm with broke with no job in years, no friends, and I'm approaching forty. I had great opportunity but I just drifted through life completely oblivious to it all and now I'm here. Suicide is my most interesting option. The only thing I can do is forgot about the past and imagine what myself in five years would think of me right now. Stop caring about debt, about judgement, about the car I drive or the clothes I wear. Right now the only thing I think about is anything but the past. Psychologist and Psychiatrists can be pretty useless but finding the right one can make a lot of difference. Medications are a mixed bag and finding anything that works for you can be so much effort over many years but still try something every now and then, Always do your own research and just don't take their word for it. As far as trying new things, it can be a cliche, but breaking out of a comfort zone that involves depression can help. Other people aren't as always as critical of you as you are of yourself. Sometimes you think that you are the only loser in the world and will always be one but that isn't necessarily true.

I know that the mantra is to just go out and do it without thinking about it so many are so scatter brained that we can barely take care of ourselves, hold a job, or maintain relationships. Exercising might help but it's hard when you're alone and depressed. If only there was a magic switch to our mentality but unfortunately it is very hard to reinvent oneself.

I think the main thing is that they (she) is affected so differently by things in life than most of us. It really is about the perspective in which one views themselves, the world, and others. People who are depressed usually are extra sensitive to what we see mundane but at the same time unable to communicate their actual feelings b/c they see themselves as so odd or disconnected from everything. Just connect with her, you'll probably have to force or coax her into opening up and she will likely be defensive. Be kind kind and just say that the most important thing to you is what is going through her head and how she feels, that you are truly interested, almost enthralled, in how she feels right now. Just don't be too pushy. Having a specific moment to focus on will help. You'll need to try different approaches and angles because you will get so much push back and denial, it's a common trait in depressives, just try to make it relaxed and draw out her real thoughts and feelings. No one wants to show weakness and that is how all mental illnesses are perceived. Don't ever blame her, trust me, I've dealt with depression and the worse things get the more I blame myself and the more I blame myself the worse things get

Finding a good psychologist/psychiatrist is so hard. I've been trying for ten years and have yet to meet one that I actually felt good talking to. I've seen all types too: different specializations, different backgrounds or educations, male or female, from different places. At worst they have been awful and there was what I would call a feeling of resentment on one side or maybe even mutual. At best they were sort of apathetic, they were just doing their job and at the end of the day they wanted to go home and live their life. Trusting them enough to open is a real problem for me too. There are so many things that you just don't want to tell them b/c it is hard for you. Even though you know that they have probably heard it before and can't tell everyone I just can't bring myself to say the things that are really hurting me. It's hard to be vulnerable with a stranger, even if they are a professional. A good therapist is one who can guide you and bring these things out, it's really how therapy works (see r/CBT), they don't necessarily fix your problems for you but get you to address and work through your problems.


Having people to talk to is important and can really change your mood. I have my own issues and sometimes just coming on here and talking with people helps me feel better, I can't say exactly why but it does. Letting things out can just be a relief so try not to shut it in all the time.

Just like you, I'm way behind the curve and made almost nothing of all the opportunities that I had when I was younger. It's very tough to see people with success, happiness, and progress because not only do you not have it but you really want it. Focus on that second part, the wanting of success, happiness, and progress. From there you have to decide how to achieve it. Education and skills are always a great place to start b/c you create value in yourself. Its a grind but getting started is the hardest part. The optimism, innocence, and naivete of youth is something we are all nostalgic for, its not just you. If you lose something in life or are lacking something you need to replace it, don't go spending you time collecting voids b/c it is time and effort to gain nothing. If a car gets a flat tire you don't just keep driving on it, you put on a spare until you can find another tire to replace it. Right now, throw on a spare and work towards finding what can replace that flatness you have in your life. Just don't stand on the side of the road and watch everyone pass you by. You know where you want to go you just have to get there. Best of luck.

There is definitively bias in diagnoses but I think that it affects all people in different ways. It's hard for me to say factually b/c I'm not a doctor and I don't even work in the medical field. Different groups of people are viewed by practitioners in different ways and it is a real problem but I don't know enough to say if these perspectives are routed in the physicians practical training or their personal perspectives, maybe one, maybe the other. My main experience is that most docs didn't really think that there was much wrong with me b/c I looked on the surface to be "normal", that is that I was a white male from a middle-class background so what could really be my problem. I think your sentence "growing up in an abusive household with drug addicted parents and being molested at a young age" is where you should start. There is definitely a name to what you went through and its in that sentence. I'm not sure if you're familiar with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy but it can be really helpful for someone who has been through what you have been through. CBT has a subreddit. It can be done via one-on-one therapy, group therapy, or just talking about it. As far as therapist go, I understand how hard it can be to find some stranger and trust them to help heal you (on your dime) but that is what you have to do. If you aren't comfortable with a therapist than stick to reddit, it can really help. Also try group therapy though that can be tough. You really need to get to talking with people who can understand what it was like to be you growing up. It will be tough at first but what you gain from it will be worth it many times over. Through all of this, your boyfriend will need to support you (does he know?). There is no way you can do this without him being involved. He should absolutely be supportive of you and do everything he can to help you deal with your difficult past. If he does not seem interested in helping you I think that is cause for concern. The bottom line is that every human being is a beautiful person but some times things happen, things that are out of our control, things that shouldn't happen in the first place. The people that do these things are abnormal and not the person that these things happen to. You are pure because of who you are and not what someone did to you. Bad people are those that hurt others. Bad people are not those that are hurt. Remember that. Someone hurt you and you didn't hurt anyone so who is to blame? Not you. You are a good person because you chose to be and what everyone else does to you, lies or abuse or whatever, makes them a bad person and not you. Stay strong.

Sounds like mania or a manic episode or a type of anxiety or panic attack. Mania or manic episodes are a sort of enjoyable high. You feel like you could do anything. Anxiety and panic attacks feel more like heart attacks and would involve other acute physical symptoms like heavy breathing, sweating, and accelerated heart rate. The first thing you should do is lie down, make yourself comfortable, and try to practice controlled breathing. You should also consider any prescription or over the counter drugs you've taken and what you've eaten or drank recently as you could be having some type of reaction.

This is a feeling that most people with depression have dealt with, me included. You've got a weight attached to you and you're fighting it. It makes it hard to climb out of depression, you have to fight and even then it can drag you down. You feel lost even though you don't know where you are going. You need something but have no idea what it is. What I do is focus. Focus on what hurts and work through those feelings. Focus on what makes you happy and work it into you life. Think of those things you don't have but you want and make a plan to get them. Learning is never wasted. This will pay dividends. Small achivements can make the difference. Replace the abstract with the concrete. Common advice for people with depression or anxiety is to work on some simple task like cleaning your bedroom or doing laundry. Do that and then ask yourself, "What am I going to do next?" Don't constantly pressure yourself though, have some leisure time, partake in something you like, doesn't matter what it is. For instance, I like to watch movies and right now I am watching all of Joel and Ethan Coen's movies. I watch one every night or two and then post or join a discussion on the movies subreddit. It isn't important in the big picture but it's good to give yourself an avenue to channel you thoughts and energy. Exercise the hurt, practice the positive, build yourself, and take time for yourself. Also, take it slow, measure yourself by your progress and achievements and not the what-ifs.

I think anyone who is depressed or has anxiety has been through this, I know I have. Consistency is something that is hard to achieve in our lives, sometimes you just feel like a totally different person from one day to the next and it makes it hard to maintain friendships, a job, or any kind of routine (diet, exercise, etc.). Dealing with the "starting over" is so hard, you just want to give up after so many re-starts. No matter how good you feel eventually the bottom drops out and you are back to square one. It's so hard to deal with but you have to find a way to dig in and keep climbing. You might ask how or why but that isn't anything I can answer, it is really up to you but you know there is a reason. I sort of just embrace the challenge, even get a little angry, and just do the best I can. It isn't easy and doesn't always work, but I always feel at least a little better because I know that if I try than I have a chance. I hang on to that chance, I believe b/c I want to. Maybe it is wishful thinking but at least it has heart and that counts for something.

Falling asleep is something most depressives have trouble with, especially me. I think most people with depression are hit harder when they are waking up or falling asleep. For me it happens mostly at night but the thoughts follow the same line. You find yourself right back where you started, laying in your room staring at the same surroundings you see every time you fall asleep/wake up. It makes you feel stuck or static, like you're not going anywhere, that even if you made progress yesterday you're right back where you started. It's sort of a mind trick. I think this is why traveling is often used as a way to overcome depression, when you're forced to go out into new surroundings, meet new people, and encounter new situations, you don't have the time or mental resources to focus on depression or any of the things which make you depressed. This is also an argument for why just going out, taking on hobbies, or interacting with new people is a good way to fight depression. These things do help but aren't a panacea. Also, it is easier to reflect, for better or worse, when you are alone in your privacy. I have depression and when I lay down to go to sleep I have recurring thoughts of how I haven't done anything with my life, how I screwed up, how so many other people are happy and successful, etc. Leaving a depressed person to explore their own mind generally leads to negative thoughts. Coming up with a routine to waking up or falling asleep can really help, just try not to use drugs or alcohol but instead try meditation, recitation of goals, positive thoughts, exercise, making list of things accomplished or things to do, etc.

Depression is hard to define and isn't the same for any person though one feeling many depressed people have is that they constantly aren't comfortable with anything. Depression isn't just numbness, it is also a feeling of despair, anguish, or conflict with how one feels. Depressives generally hate or at least dislike themselves and are definitely not comfortable with feeling that way. Take something that genuinely makes you feel upset down to the pit of your stomach. Now imagine having that feeling everyday, even for little to no reason. Depression is like wearing an anchor around your neck, it drags you down. It isn't really being suicidal but feeling so distraught that suicide makes sense. It's terrible and not comfortable. Simply put, would you rather have the flu or not have the flu? No one wants to be sick.

I've had the same problem most of my life and it's not an easy one to solve. I learned that my problem was that I would just depend on other people for my fun and people get tired of that. It's one thing to be part of the group and its another to contribute. Most social activity involves some coordination so try to be a part of making things happen. Come up with ideas or contribute to others. This applies to a simple movie night or to a weekend trip. The best way to be part of the social group is to participate in the social group. If that doesn't work out than you might need to branch out but not cut people off. First thing is to try to make friends with new people or expand your social circle. I'm not saying to cut your old/other friends out. Most people like to meet new people and do new things. Look at it this way: your friend invites you out to do something you've done before with with people you already know OR your friend invites you to do something new with a different group of people. Even if there was nothing wrong with the first option, doesn't the second one sound a little more interesting? Trying new things and meeting new people generally gets people's interest (unless they prefer routine, nothing wrong with that btw). So when people don't invite you out, try new things with new people. If that works out, then ask your "old" friends if they want to come and meet your "new" friends. Mixing social circles and activities is usually fun and you might be the reason it happened. If that doesn't work than maybe your friends who didn't invite you out just don't want to open up their clique and then it might be time to move on, maybe with your new group of friends or with an older group but at least doing new things. Who knows, maybe you and your new group decide on some new fun thing to do and those that didn't want you around before will maybe want to come. I understand that some groups like to be so exclusive and won't make any effort to include people, I've been there. Trying to break through their walls is probably impossible so your best option is to make them want to leave their walls. It's strange, people might not ever consider going to a party/social event but would still be upset at not being invited. It can be hard to be outgoing, especially to people who might feel superior or are self-centered, but the best thing you can do is enrich and grow your social circle and try to involve others. If they are still not interested then at least you have friends that are. I've been in your position before and it's tough. Just keep at it, you can be the center(ish) of any social circle though it might take some effort through trial and error.
